name: Carol Mack
life: “I still remember recognizing a person's laugh before their changing face.” On Monday, near the window at Night Shift Donuts, Carol knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I met her during treatment and have never seen the woman her friends keep insisting she used to be.
appearance: Carol is easy to recognize by short sandy hair and a marked widow's peak and a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Usually dressed in a dark green knitted vest with a braided bracelet with a single wooden bead, Carol folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing when listening.
personality: Carol has a quick wit and an equally quick sense of shame. A joke is often Carol's way of finding out whether a room is friendly enough for a serious question.
agenda: To meet the person already known without comparison to the past.
family: Alice Ortiz is Carol’s second cousin. Carol asks what the birthday guest would like this year. Alice remembers the birthdays. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *The engine lullaby*, Alice says, “My father took me aboard whenever I couldn't sleep.”
connections: Ramon Lloyd. Someone who only knew the client during illness notices the barber's changing hair too.

reactions.response: Carol waits for the customer's permission before anyone takes a picture.

reactions.situation: A customer is short at the till while a queue forms
reactions.response: Carol keeps the customer's place while they check the amount and gets the impatient people talking about something else.

reactions.response: Carol seeks out the person it hurt before telling anybody why it was supposed to be funny.
reactions.asWritten: If the joke lands badly, Carol seeks out the person it hurt before telling anybody why it was supposed to be funny.
